## Result — how accounting for academic characteristics alters the SES and race associations

**Outcome language (as instructed): post-secondary attendance / BA-track progress.** Nothing here describes a completed bachelor's degree — the file has no credential variable. Primary `y_O3` = grade ≥13 by 1979 **or** dorm/frat/sorority residence 1981–88 (2,481 events, 19.8% of 12,532); side-by-side `y_O1` (grade≥13), `y_O2` (dorm), and the named sensitivity `y_PROSP` (baseline grade ≤12 → dorm 1982–88). Logit with HC1; LPM/OLS HC1 in the same table; KHB-style scale-corrected attenuation; reference NON-BLACK NON-HISPANIC; sex + age1979 in all models from M1. Script re-run clean from scratch (exit 0); all 23 summary numbers re-checked against the regenerated CSVs (all OK).

### 1. Primary ladder (y_O3) — N/events at each step
| model | N | events | Black AOR [95% CI] | Hispanic AOR [95% CI] | parent-ed AOR/yr | pseudo-R² |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| M0 race | 12,532 | 2,481 | 0.462 [0.399, 0.534]* | 0.680 [0.610, 0.757]* | – | 0.012 |
| M1 +sex+age | 12,532 | 2,481 | 0.486 [0.420, 0.563]* | 0.711 [0.637, 0.793]* | – | 0.037 |
| **A +SES** | 12,098 | 2,453 | 0.989 [0.840, 1.165] ns | 1.044 [0.928, 1.173] ns | 1.327 [1.301, 1.353]* | 0.134 |
| **B +ASVAB×4** | 10,653 | 2,277 | **1.483 [1.216, 1.808]*** | **2.821 [2.413, 3.297]*** | 1.178 [1.151, 1.206]* | 0.273 |
| B_comp (ASVAB mean) | 10,653 | 2,277 | 1.594 [1.311, 1.937]* | 3.204 [2.750, 3.734]* | 1.184 [1.157, 1.211]* | 0.258 |

Variants (Black/Hispanic AOR, A→B): y_O1 1.482/1.058→2.457/3.083; y_O2 0.620/1.115→0.871/2.736; y_PROSP 0.574/1.103→0.807/2.722. Categorical SES (matched N=11,008): parent 16+ vs ≤11 12.8→4.4; any-parent-BA 5.38→2.87. 1978 log income 1.170*→1.052 ns. 1985 wealth (post-decision, exploratory): 1.000 ns→0.992 ns. Class rank (separate model, N=5,461): rank percentile AOR 17.4*, but SES moves only 1.285→1.240 and Black 0.928→0.993.

### 2. A→B attenuation (SES and race only)
| outcome | term | β_A | β_total(KHB) | β_B | %naive | %scale-corrected | %AME | sig A→B |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| y_O3 | parent ed | 0.2913 | 0.2402 | 0.1636 | **−43.8** | **−31.9** | −53.0 | * → * |
| y_O3 | Black | −0.0431 ns | −0.0355 | +0.3938* | n/a¹ | n/a¹ | n/a¹ | ns → **\*** |
| y_O3 | Hispanic | +0.0452 ns | +0.0373 | +1.0370* | n/a¹ | n/a¹ | n/a¹ | ns → **\*** |
| y_O1 | parent ed | 0.2841 | 0.2055 | 0.1610 | −43.3 | −21.7 | −52.5 | * → * |
| y_O2 | parent ed | 0.2765 | 0.2368 | 0.1444 | −47.8 | −39.1 | −53.5 | * → * |
| y_O2 | Black | −0.4475 | −0.3833 | −0.1383 | −69.1 | −63.9 | −72.5 | * → ns |
| y_PROSP | parent ed | 0.2893 | 0.2484 | 0.1529 | −47.1 | −38.4 | −52.9 | * → * |
| y_PROSP | Black | −0.5438 | −0.4670 | −0.2143 | −60.6 | −54.1 | −64.9 | * → ns |

¹ **Reported plainly, as you asked:** percent change is uninterpretable for the race coefficients because Model A's are numerically ~0 — the raw table shows −1,014%/+2,194%. Absolute changes are +0.44 (Black) and +0.99 (Hispanic) log-odds. **The two measures disagree in magnitude for SES on y_O1 (−43% naive vs −22% corrected, 22pp apart)** and by 8–9pp on y_O2/y_PROSP; signs and significance never disagree (SES p<1e-10 in both models). **Logit vs LPM also disagree in 12 of 56 cells** — mostly opposite signs on sub-1pp near-zero race contrasts, but two are material: y_O3 Model A Black (logit 0.99 ns vs LPM +0.033, p=.005) and y_O2/y_PROSP Model B Black (logit ~0.87–0.93 ns vs LPM +0.018/+0.022, p<.01). Those I call statistically ambiguous, not directional.

Scale-stable g-computed risk differences (y_O3): Black−NBH −10.9pp raw → −10.0pp (M1) → **−0.2pp (A)** → **+4.4pp (B) / +5.4pp (B_comp)**; Hispanic −6.1 → −5.3 → +0.6 → **+12.8/+14.8pp**. Parent-ed 16+ vs ≤8: **+32.8pp → +17.0pp**; parent-BA vs none +32.2 → +15.2pp.

### 3. Descriptive cross-tabs (the crux)
Attended %, race × ASVAB quartile (n=10,653): Q1 3.8/6.9/2.3; Q2 9.0/18.7/4.9; Q3 18.3/36.7/19.0; Q4 39.8/54.1/49.3 (BLACK/HISPANIC/NBH) → the Black−NBH gap goes **+1.5, +4.1, −0.7, −9.6pp**; Hispanic−NBH **+4.6, +13.8, +17.7, +4.8pp**. By parental education: at ≤8/9–11 years all groups sit at 5–9% with gaps within ±2.5pp; at 13–15 and 16+ the NBH rate (33.7%, 54.0%) exceeds BLACK (20.0%, 33.1%) by 13.7 and **20.9pp** — the SES gap not only persists at high parental education, it widens. The three-way table confirms why Model B reverses sign: within ASVAB tertile *and* parental education, BLACK ≥ NBH in 5 of 9 cells and HISPANIC in 8 of 9 (both fall below NBH only in the ASVAB-high/parent-13+ cell, where NBH hits 57.3%). Mean ASVAB at parent-ed 16+: NBH +0.91, BLACK +0.51, HISPANIC +0.10 SD.

### 4. Missingness
ASVAB 12.2% (13.4% non-attenders vs 7.3% attenders; NBH 14.2%, BLACK 11.4%, HISP 7.8%), max-parental-ed 3.5% (4.0% vs 1.1%), class rank 55.6% (61.3% vs 32.7%), 1978 income 19.6%, 1985 wealth 20.4%. P(ASVAB missing): OR 0.59 Black, 0.48 Hispanic, 0.94/parental-ed year, 1.18/age year → **MAR-violating**. Mean-imputation + indicators (N 10,653→12,532): Black 1.59→1.53, Hispanic 3.20→2.69, parent-ed 1.184→1.188; indicator itself AOR 0.70. **Likely direction of bias: complete-case analysis modestly inflates the positive Model-B race coefficients and slightly understates the SES gradient, because attenders are over-represented among rows with observed ASVAB; qualitative conclusions unchanged.**

### Two qualifications I added rather than buried
1. **The Model-A "no race gap" is functional-form dependent.** The SES gradient is flat below grade 12 and steep above (7.7%, 7.7%, 16.5%, 31.8%, 45.3%, 61.0% by parent-ed band) and parental education is very differently distributed by race (mean 9.1 years BLACK vs 11.9 NBH). Black AOR on y_O3: 0.96 (linear pe, p=.62) / 0.82 (categorical, p=.03) / 0.87 (quadratic, p=.12). For y_O2 and y_PROSP the Model-A Black deficit is robust (0.51–0.65, all p<.001).
2. **Strong race × parental-education interaction:** Black×pe AOR 0.80/yr (p<1e-6) on y_O3, 0.79 on y_O2, 0.74 on y_PROSP; Hispanic×pe 0.94 (p=.016). The Black deficit widens with parental education — that is what makes the main effect "disappear" when the interaction is ignored.

Robustness: the reversal and SES attenuation survive age dummies (Black 0.97→1.62), each ASVAB score singly (1.27–1.45), available-item mean (1.59), +family size (1.55), age≥18 restriction (1.27→2.45); VIFs 2.7–3.4.

### Guardrails honored
A→B is presented as descriptive composition/decomposition, not causal adjustment: ASVAB/class rank are 1981 measures that partly post-date the 1979 grade-based outcome and are themselves socially patterned (r=0.48 with parental education). In the correctly-ordered `y_PROSP` variant the Black gap shrinks but does **not** reverse (AOR 0.574*→0.807 ns, −6.0pp→−3.0pp g-computed), while the Hispanic advantage appears as soon as scores are held constant. The composite inherits much of its racial pattern from the dorm component, a residential-selection proxy. No survey weights; race is near-collinear with sample strata.

### FINAL HYPOTHESIS (submitted answer, worded to the observable outcome)
Accounting for academic characteristics changes the two background effects in opposite directions. In NLSY79, post-secondary attendance / BA-track progress is overwhelmingly predicted by family SES — each extra year of the better-educated parent's schooling multiplies the odds by 1.33 (95% CI 1.30–1.35; +33 percentage points comparing ≤8 with ≥16 parental years) — and adding parental education alone absorbs essentially all of the unadjusted racial gaps (Black −10.9pp, Hispanic −6.1pp, both reduced to about zero and non-significant). Adding 1981 ASVAB scores then attenuates the SES association by about a third of its log-odds (AOR 1.33→1.18; −44% naive, −32% scale-corrected, −53% of the marginal effect; the parent-college advantage halves from +32pp to +17pp) while leaving it large and highly significant, whereas the race coefficients do not attenuate — they reverse (Black 0.96→1.59, Hispanic 1.05→3.20; +5pp and +15pp adjusted risk differences). Thus academic characteristics account for a substantial share of the socioeconomic gradient but none of the racial gap: minority respondents with equal parental schooling and equal test scores were at least as likely as non-black non-Hispanic peers to progress to post-secondary education. The racial divide that survives adjustment is unequal academic preparation (mean ASVAB at parent-ed 16+: +0.91 NBH vs +0.51 Black vs +0.10 Hispanic SD) plus a race×SES interaction (Black×parent-ed AOR 0.80/yr, p<1e-6) showing the Black deficit widening at high parental education. The Hispanic advantage is the most robust finding (AOR 2.6–3.3 on the composite, 2.7–3.1 in the prospective variant); the Black coefficient is outcome- and specification-sensitive (1.0–1.6 composite, 2.4–2.6 grade-only, ~0.9 or below on college residence) and should not be reported as a settled directional result. This is a descriptive composition/decomposition, not a causal estimate.

payload.hypothesis: Accounting for academic characteristics changes the two background effects in opposite directions. In NLSY79, post-secondary attendance / BA-track progress (highest grade >= 13 by 1979, or dorm/fraternity/sorority residence in 1981-88; 19.8% of 12,532 respondents) is overwhelmingly predicted by family SES - each extra year of the better-educated parent's schooling raises the odds by a factor of 1.33 (95% CI 1.30-1.35; +33 percentage points comparing parents with <=8 versus >=16 years) - and adding parental education alone absorbs essentially all of the unadjusted racial gaps (Black -10.9pp, Hispanic -6.1pp, both reduced to about zero and non-significant). Adding 1981 ASVAB test scores then attenuates the SES effect by roughly a third of its log-odds (AOR 1.33 -> 1.18; -44% naive, -32% KHB scale-corrected, -53% of the average marginal effect; the parent-college advantage halves from +32pp to +17pp) while leaving it large and highly significant, whereas the race coefficients do not attenuate at all - they reverse: Black AOR 0.96 -> 1.59 and Hispanic 1.05 -> 3.20 (+5pp and +15pp adjusted risk differences). So academic characteristics account for a substantial share of the socioeconomic gradient but none of the racial gap: minority respondents with equal parental schooling and equal test scores were at least as likely as their non-black non-Hispanic peers to progress to post-secondary education. What survives adjustment as the real racial divide is unequal academic preparation (mean ASVAB composite at parent education 16+: NB NON-HISP +0.91, BLACK +0.51, HISPANIC +0.10 SD units), together with a race x SES interaction (Black x parent-ed AOR 0.80/yr, p<1e-6) showing the Black deficit widening at high parental education. The Hispanic advantage is the most robust single finding (ASVAB-adjusted AOR 2.6-3.3 on the composite outcome, 2.7-3.1 in the correctly temporally-ordered prospective variant, significant in every specification); the Black ASVAB-adjusted coefficient is much less stable (1.0-1.6 on the composite, 2.4-2.6 on the 1979-grade outcome, ~0.9 or below and statistically ambiguous on college residence and the prospective variant). This is a descriptive composition/decomposition, not a causal estimate: ASVAB and class rank are 1981 measures that partly post-date the 1979 attainment measure and are themselves socially patterned (r = 0.48 with parental education), and the outcome is observed post-secondary attendance / BA-track progress, not a completed degree.
payload.workflow: Read-only inspection then pre-registered analysis of data/nls_raw.csv (12,686 x 61). Outcomes: y_O1 grade>=13 (1979); y_O2 dorm/frat/sorority 1981-88; y_O3 = y_O1 OR y_O2 (PRIMARY, 19.8%); y_PROSP = baseline grade<=12 -> dorm 1982-88 (prospective sensitivity). Code 95 in highest-grade treated as sentinel. SES = max(mother, father) years (linear, categorical <=11/12/13-15/16+, any-parent-BA); 1978 log income as sensitivity; 1985 signed log wealth exploratory and flagged as post-decision. Race = dummies vs NON-BLACK NON-HISPANIC; sex and age1979 in every model from M1. Academic block = the four 1981 ASVAB scores re-standardised (columns are mislabelled 'Z'; actual mean ~476, SD ~100) or their composite; class-rank percentile = 1-(rank-0.5)/class size kept in a separate reduced-coverage model (55.6% missing). Ladder M0 -> M1 -> A (+SES) -> B (+academic) fitted for 4 outcomes x 15 specifications with statsmodels Logit (HC1) and OLS (HC1), average marginal effects, and KHB-style scale-corrected attenuation on identical samples (Var(y*) = Var(Xb_big) + pi^2/3; k = (pi/sqrt3)/sigma_small). Also: g-computed standardised race and SES risk differences, descriptive race x ASVAB and race x parental-education cross-tabs (2- and 3-way), missingness diagnostics and a missingness-mechanism logit, mean-imputation + indicator sensitivity, logit-vs-LPM sign/significance agreement audit, SES functional-form and race x SES interaction audit, and robustness checks (age dummies, single ASVAB scores, available-item mean, family size, age>=18, VIF). Deliverables: analysis/nls_analysis.py and 12 files in results/.
